ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Cardiology (heart failure) Referral — Duke Kahanamoku

code.originalText: Establishing care for six weeks of breathlessness, ankle swelling and tiredness five years after a heart attack: examination, ECG, chest X-ray, NT-proBNP and laboratory tests, a diuretic, and the plan for an echocardiogram

text.paragraph: Six weeks of breathlessness, ankle swelling and tiredness in a 66-year-old Native Hawaiian man five years after a heart attack, with NT-proBNP 2,450 pg/mL, old anterior Q waves and an enlarged heart on chest X-ray. Please confirm the diagnosis and cause, advise on guideline-directed medical therapy and its order, the ischemic evaluation and device decisions, and how he can return to swimming and surfing safely. [S]
Urgency: Soon; on the day of his two-week visit, after the echocardiogram that morning. [S]

list.item: Does he have heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, and is the cause ischemic?
Does he need an ischemic evaluation, and could revascularization help?
Which guideline-directed medicines should he start, in what order, and how should lisinopril and metoprolol tartrate be changed?
Should his iron deficiency be treated, and how?
When should a defibrillator or resynchronization device be considered?
How and when can he safely return to swimming and surfing?

text.paragraph: Sheriff of Honolulu and a lifelong swimmer and surfer; never smoked or drank. Heart attack five years ago treated with medicines; on aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, metoprolol tartrate 25 mg twice daily and lisinopril 10 mg since then. Six weeks of breathlessness on slopes and while paddling, two-pillow orthopnea, evening ankle swelling and tiredness; NYHA class III. Today blood pressure 142/86, pulse 92, oxygen saturation 94%; jugular venous pressure 6 cm, basal crackles, 2+ ankle edema, soft S3. ECG: sinus rhythm, Q waves in V1 to V4, QRS 104 ms. Chest X-ray: enlarged heart, venous diversion, small effusions. NT-proBNP 2,450 pg/mL; sodium 138, potassium 4.2 mmol/L, creatinine 1.02 mg/dL (eGFR 81); hemoglobin 13.4 g/dL; ferritin 62 ng/mL, transferrin saturation 16%; TSH 2.1; hemoglobin A1c 5.9%; LDL 92 mg/dL. Started furosemide 40 mg daily and raised atorvastatin to 80 mg today. He wants his ʻohana involved in decisions as he chooses, and he makes the decisions [S]

list.item: He wants to get back in the ocean, to swim and surf again. [S]
He wants to keep working as sheriff. [S]
He wants his ʻohana involved as he chooses and his own ways of healing respected. [S]

text.paragraph: Historical basis. These claims are historical evidence, not findings from a modern examination.

list.item: Duke Kahanamoku was born on August 24, 1890, in Honolulu, at Haleʻākala, the Honolulu home of Princess Bernice Pauahi Bishop; he was named after his father, who had been named Duke for a visit of the Duke of Edinburgh to Hawaiʻi. [D]
Olympedia gives his full name as Duke Paoa Kahino Makoe Hulikohoa Kahanamoku. [D]

He won the Olympic 100-meter freestyle in 1912 at Stockholm (with silver in the 4 x 200-meter relay) and again in 1920 at Antwerp (with gold in the relay), and silver in the 100-meter freestyle in 1924 at Paris: three gold and two silver medals. [D]

He co-founded the Hui Nalu surf club in 1911, introduced surfing to the Atlantic coast of the United States in 1914 and gave a surfing exhibition at Freshwater Beach in Sydney on December 24, 1914, widely regarded as a seminal event for surfing in Australia; he was inducted into the International Swimming Hall of Fame in 1965 and was the first inductee of the International Surfing Hall of Fame in 1966. [D]
From 1922 he lived in Los Angeles for years and found small roles in many Hollywood films. [D]

He was elected sheriff of Honolulu for 13 consecutive terms, from 1934 until the post was eliminated in 1960, after which he was named Hawaiʻi's "Ambassador of Aloha"; other sources date his first election to 1932 and his departure to 1961. [D]
He married Nadine Alexander on August 2, 1940, in Kailua-Kona. [D]
He never drank alcohol or smoked and trained consistently. [D]
He had a heart attack in 1952 and suffered several heart attacks in his later years, continuing to swim and sail almost to the end of his life. [D]
He had no great personal wealth. [D]
He was the official United States representative at the 1956 Melbourne Olympic Games. [D]

Culturally safe care: address him as Mr. Kahanamoku, as he asked; take time; explain each test and medicine plainly; involve his ʻohana as he chooses while he makes the decisions. Guideline: Potentially Preventable Hospitalizations for Congestive Heart Failure Among Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders in Hawaiʻi (2015); Ke Ola Mamo: a Native Hawaiian Health Care System serving Oʻahu (medical care, lomilomi and community health workers) (2026) [S]

Furosemide 40 mg every morning for congestion, with a daily weight and a written plan; metabolic panel and magnesium in one to two weeks; lower the dose when he is dry. Guideline: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure (2022); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, heart failure and ischemic heart disease monographs (2026) [S]

Baseline tests: ECG, chest X-ray, NT-proBNP, metabolic panel and magnesium, blood count, iron studies, TSH, hemoglobin A1c, lipids and ALT; echocardiogram at the two-week visit. Guideline: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure (2022); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, heart failure and ischemic heart disease monographs (2026) [S]

Atorvastatin raised from 40 to 80 mg for LDL 92 mg/dL; lipid panel in four to twelve weeks; goal below 70 mg/dL. Guideline: 2023 AHA/ACC/ACCP/ASPC/NLA/PCNA Guideline for the Management of Patients With Chronic Coronary Disease (2023); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, heart failure and ischemic heart disease monographs (2026) [S]

Sodium: less salted and dried fish, shoyu and salty party food, using the foods he already eats; no routine fluid restriction; daily weights. Guideline: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure (2022) [S]

Vaccinations: pneumococcal, influenza, COVID-19 and RSV as due, because heart disease raises the risk of severe respiratory infection. Guideline: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure (2022); Adult Immunization Schedule by Age (2026) [S]

Native Hawaiian healing alongside clinic care, if he wishes: lomilomi through Ke Ola Mamo, a Native Hawaiian Health Care System; he will tell the clinic before using any plant medicine so that interactions can be checked; the clinic asks nothing further about his practices. Guideline: Ke Ola Mamo: a Native Hawaiian Health Care System serving Oʻahu (medical care, lomilomi and community health workers) (2026) [S]
